Project Data, Persistence, Recovery, and Migration Plan

purpose: Ensure V2 can evolve its data model without losing projects or weakening the current strong persistence safeguards.
evidence: Current serializer uses schema version 2, strict type checks, invariant validation, atomic writes, and future-schema rejection.
Current recovery and relink behavior intentionally allows missing media while rejecting structurally invalid projects.
decisions: Project schema changes require explicit forward migration functions and regression fixtures.
Never silently discard unknown future data.
Animation/keyframe V2 data must be introduced with backward migration from current AnimationAssignment semantics.
Keep media paths relocatable and relink-friendly for portable workflows.
tasks: Define schema version 3 only after final V2 model is approved.
Create migration pipeline v1 -> v2 -> v3 with idempotence and failure boundaries.
Add project backup before irreversible migration and a clear rollback message.
Define stable identifiers for scenes/assets/effects if richer editing requires moving/reordering scenes.
Define autosave/recovery cadence and crash-recovery selection logic.
Add corruption fixtures, truncated JSON, unexpected types, duplicate IDs, missing assets, unsupported future versions, and migration round-trip tests.
Define privacy boundaries for metadata and provider information.
gate: PASS when all existing valid project fixtures open successfully in V2.
PASS when migrations are deterministic and tested both success/failure paths.
PASS when a migration failure cannot overwrite the original project.
PASS when future schemas are rejected safely rather than guessed.

UI/UX Parity and Professional Evolution Plan

purpose: Keep the established white/blue professional UI and current feature placement recognizable while improving clarity, responsiveness, and mature editing feedback.
evidence: Current product is based on 42 canonical UI references and a 1920x1080 reference viewport.
The user explicitly wants UI/features to remain the same conceptually; mature external repos are for stability/engine ideas, not for replacing the product identity.
decisions: V2 begins from current UI parity; no wholesale redesign.
Any layout change must solve a documented usability or technical problem.
Backend capability changes must be reflected through disabled/hidden controls and explanations, not silent failure.
Prompt/image UI design work, if later required, becomes its own gated phase before UI implementation.
tasks: Capture baseline screenshots of all major screens at reference resolution and representative smaller Windows scaling settings.
Create a UI inventory mapping controls to application commands and feature status.
Improve status/progress/error surfaces for render, AI jobs, missing tools, unsupported effects, and project migration.
Standardize spacing, typography, disabled state, hover/focus, keyboard navigation, and destructive action confirmation.
Define performance UX: skeleton/loading states, background job panel, non-blocking progress, cancel/retry buttons.
Plan accessibility checks: contrast, focus order, keyboard access, scalable text, screen-reader labels where practical.
Preserve existing white/blue visual identity and compact professional editor density.
gate: PASS when current workflows remain recognizable and all major commands are mapped.
PASS when UI does not expose capabilities the active backend cannot deliver.
PASS when screenshot regression tests cover critical screens.
PASS when no generated UI reference is implemented without prior approval in the designated UI gate.

Performance, Cache, Preview, and Resource Management Plan

purpose: Improve responsiveness for large projects without introducing unsafe caching or memory leaks.
evidence: Current preview and render paths are deliberately separate and not claimed as frame-perfect WYSIWYG.
External mature libraries show that caching can help or hurt depending on workload; therefore V2 must benchmark rather than assume.
decisions: Cache keys must be content/configuration derived and safely invalidated.
Preview can use reduced-resolution/proxy strategies as long as timing/geometry intent remains correct and final render is unaffected.
Resource limits must be explicit for concurrent jobs, decoded frames, thumbnails, and caches.
tasks: Define benchmark projects at 10/100/500 scenes and representative 1080p/4K assets.
Measure startup, project load, thumbnail generation, seek latency, playback smoothness, memory peak, render throughput, cancellation latency, and package size.
Plan thumbnail/proxy generation with bounded LRU cache and background priority.
Define job concurrency policy by CPU/RAM and prevent render+AI+thumbnail work from starving UI.
Add leak/regression tests for repeated open/close, seek loops, re-render, and provider jobs.
Define diagnostic mode that records timing and backend information without user secrets.
gate: PASS when V2 has baseline benchmark numbers before optimization.
PASS when each cache has ownership, size limit, key, invalidation, and cleanup policy.
PASS when large-project operations remain cancellable and UI-responsive.
risks: Optimizing synthetic cases instead of real workflows

Testing, QA, Security, and Regression Strategy

purpose: Turn the old app's existing quality gates into stricter V2 acceptance gates that cover multiple backends, migration, UI, and Windows runtime behavior.
evidence: Existing project already uses Ruff, strict mypy, pytest, CodeQL, screenshot checks, real Windows packaging, and real FFmpeg integration tests.
decisions: Existing passing tests become a minimum regression floor, not a disposable suite.
Every V2 bug fix requires a regression test when technically feasible.
Backend parity requires integration/golden tests, not only unit tests.
Security checks include credentials, subprocess arguments, path handling, downloaded/native dependencies, and release provenance.
tasks: Create test pyramid: pure domain/unit, application command, adapter integration, render golden, UI smoke/screenshot, packaging, end-to-end Windows.

Add adversarial fixtures for malformed DOCX/SRT/project JSON, Unicode/long paths, corrupt credentials, missing tools, interrupted renders, provider timeouts, invalid media, and low-disk scenarios where feasible.
Define golden-frame tolerances for animation effects and exact timing tolerances for audio/subtitles.
Add dependency/license/SBOM checks for newly bundled libraries.
Add performance regression thresholds to CI for selected deterministic microbenchmarks; keep heavy benchmarks scheduled/manual if needed.
Define release blocker severity levels and triage rules.
gate: PASS when legacy regression suite remains green after each implementation wave.
PASS when every selected optional backend has Windows integration coverage before default activation.
PASS when secret scanning and credential tests prove raw keys are not persisted/logged.
PASS when final candidate passes portable smoke, real render, project migration, UI smoke, and rollback checks.
